text:
elaine: Heads-up — CedarBank's vendor risk team just asked for an access-control evidence bundle for their SIG review. They want: a sample SAML assertion showing attribute->role mapping, an RBAC export (YAML), evidence of service-account key rotation + revoke process, session TTL defaults, and a one-row audit proving MFA was enforced. Can we turn around a ZIP by EOD?

samir: I can grab SAML + MFA proof. Quick summary to include in the pack: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC; for Hosted tenants we recommend IdP-enforced MFA and we default to requiring MFA for org admins. We record authn_context/amr and an explicit mfa=true flag in audit events. I'll paste a compact sample assertion below. :lock:

morgan: I'll produce the RBAC YAML and the service-account rotation blurb. Implementation note: service accounts issue short-lived JWTs by default (3600s) and can be constrained via allow_pattern (path prefix). Signing keys are KMS-managed for Hosted (or HSM for Private) with automated rotation; tokens are revocable immediately via the revocation API.

karen: Session defaults we should state: console idle timeout = 45m (customer-configurable), interactive shell/session = 60m, API tokens expire after 900s (refresh_token supported). Breakglass = time-limited creds + two approver flow with elevated audit markers.

elaine: Good. Please include: 1) sample SAML AttributeStatement XML, 2) RBAC YAML snippet, 3) curl to pull one MFA=true audit row, 4) one-paragraph rotation + revoke text we can paste into SIG answers, and 5) upload link from infra-bot when ZIP ready.

samir: Sample SAML AttributeStatement (compact example):

```
<AttributeStatement>
  <Attribute Name=\"email\"><AttributeValue>${user.email}</AttributeValue></Attribute>
  <Attribute Name=\"groups\"><AttributeValue>${user.groups}</AttributeValue></Attribute>
  <Attribute Name=\"entitlements\"><AttributeValue>redwood:runtime-deployer</AttributeValue></Attribute>
  <Attribute Name=\"authnContext\"><AttributeValue>urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:TimeSyncToken</AttributeValue></Attribute>
</AttributeStatement>
```

morgan: RBAC YAML snippet (minimal least-privilege example):

```
roles:
  - id: model-reader
    permissions:
      - models:read
      - logs:read
  - id: deployer
    permissions:
      - deployments:create
      - deployments:update
service_accounts:
  - id: cedarbank-poc-sa
    scopes: [\"models.read\"]
    token_ttl_seconds: 3600
    allow_pattern: \"/v1/models/cedar-*\"
```

samir: Curl to fetch one MFA-auth success (org-admin token required):

```
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" \"https://console.redwood/api/v1/audit?filter=event:authentication.success AND mfa:true&limit=1\"
```

infra-bot: audit-export ready: /exports/cedarbank/mfa_row_1933332100.csv (presigned link active 48h)

morgan: Rotation + revoke paragraph (paste-ready): \"Service-account credentials are issued as short-lived JWTs (default 3600s) or mTLS certs (Dedicated/Private). Signing keys are stored in KMS (Hosted) or HSM (Private) and rotated automatically (ephemeral/signing keys weekly, root keys monthly). Tokens and certificates can be revoked immediately via the revocation API; all rotation and revocation events are recorded in the audit log and are available for export.\"

karen: Also include a short token-scoping example we can show them (JWT claims):

```
{\"iss\":\"https://auth.redwood\",\"sub\":\"svc:cedarbank-poc\",\"scope\":\"models.read\",\"exp\":1712345678,\"aud\":\"https://api.redwood\"}
```

elaine: Perfect — once infra-bot uploads the ZIP with the SAML XML, RBAC YAML, rotation text, and the audit CSV link I'll review and send to CedarBank. Thanks team! :thumbsup:
